title: Feature branches
summary: Exercise 2: branch off develop, name it right, commit twice.

say.never: A **branch** is your own line of work that doesn't disturb anyone else's. `main` always holds the finished, tested robot code. `develop` collects finished features. Each new feature gets its own branch, and when it's done it joins `develop`.
say.bit: A branch is your own line of work. `main` stays production-ready, `develop` collects finished features, and each feature gets its own branch.

board.code:
main      o----------------------o   (only finished, tested work)
develop   o-------o--------o-----o   (features merge in here)
issue-12       \--o--o--/          (your work, off develop)

say.never: Your branch starts from `develop`, so it begins with the team's latest finished work. Name it after what you're working on, in the pattern `issue-<number>-<what it does>`, like `issue-12-turbo-boost`.
say.bit: Start from `develop` and name it `issue-<number>-<what it does>`.

say.never: Open **Source Control** (the branch icon on the left). Each exercise folder has its own section there. Click **02-feature-branch** so the buttons and menus work on that folder.
say.bit: In Source Control, click **02-feature-branch** so the buttons act on it.

say.never: Click the branch name in the bottom-left corner and choose **Create new branch from...**. Type your branch name (starting with `issue-12-`), press **Enter**, then pick `develop` as the starting point.
say.bit: Click the branch name (bottom-left), **Create new branch from...**, name it `issue-12-...`, start from `develop`.

hint.never: create a branch starting with issue-12- off develop.

say.never: Look at the bottom-left corner. It shows which branch you're on right now. It's the fastest way to check before you save work, so you don't commit to the wrong branch.
say.bit: The bottom-left corner shows the branch the editor is looking at. It's the quickest check before you commit.

say.never: The exercise wants **two separate** commits: small commits, each with a clear message, tell the story of the work. Edit `FEATURES.md` and save, stage it with the **+**, write a message and press **Commit**. Then change the file again and repeat with a new message.
say.bit: The exercise wants **two separate** commits: edit, save, stage with **+**, message, **Commit**, then do it again.

board.code:
1. edit + save FEATURES.md
2. + (stage)   3. message   4. Commit
repeat with a new message

say.never: Open the **Graph** in Source Control: your two commits sit on top of the starting one, on your `issue-12-...` branch.
say.bit: The Graph in Source Control shows your two commits on `issue-12-...`.
